result.summary: In 2026 Sutskever testified at the Musk v. Altman trial (May), received the NAS Award (April), announced a partnership with Nvidia (July) and posted a warning on X about rogue AI agents and neoclouds (around September 1). None of the pages I opened shows him attaching a date or span to an AI forecast. reply_text:
I found no dated AI prediction from Ilya Sutskever in 2026. He was in the news a lot, but nothing he said or wrote that year, on any page I opened, names a date or a span for what AI will do.

- **The "5 to 20 years" forecast is from 2025.** Much of the 2026 coverage repeats it, but it comes from his Dwarkesh Patel podcast interview, which Sutskever gave to Dwarkesh Patel early on November 26th (2025). I only saw that interview in secondary write-ups, not in a transcript.
- **The "AI will do all the things that we can do" line is also from 2025.** TechRadar ran it as a "quote of the day" in September 2026, but it comes from his speech after receiving the University of Toronto honorary degree, June 6, 2025.
- **The warning about rogue AI agents and "neoclouds" (GPU rental providers) is from 2026, but it isn't a candidate.** It was an X post, reported on September 2, 2026. OfficeChai paraphrases it: "the next time an AI agent goes rogue, it's going to try seizing control of one of these providers to run more copies of itself." That doesn't name a date or a span, and I only saw it in news reports. His X page didn't open.
- **The Nvidia press release (July 27, 2026) has a quote from him, but it's about business.** He said "We have research that is worthy of scaling up, and having access to a big NVIDIA computer will let us do so". That's about computing power and has no date.
- **The court testimony (May 11, 2026) was about OpenAI's history and his stake in the company, not forecasts.** The Reuters article on Yahoo didn't load past its first line, so I couldn't check the full text.
- **Rumours about SSI releasing a first model in August 2026 came from other people.** Nobody quoted Sutskever saying it.

I used 11 of the 12 searches and 5 of the 6 page openings.
